title: Fresh installs require a globally writable npm prefix
reasoning: When ClawPatch is absent, the installer uses `npm install --global`. On common system Node.js installations, the global prefix is owned by root, so an ordinary user cannot complete installation even though the script otherwise defaults to user-owned locations under `$HOME`. This also makes an installer run with elevated privileges modify system-wide state.
reproduction: Run the installer as a non-root user with distro-provided npm, a root-owned global npm prefix, and no existing `clawpatch` command; npm exits with a permissions error.
recommendation: Install the pinned ClawPatch package under `install_root`, as is already done for ClawHub, validate its local executable, and link it into `bin_dir`.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked to this feature, and this failure requires exercising the installer with a root-owned npm global prefix.
suggestedRegressionTest: Run the installer with a fake npm whose global installation fails as unwritable but whose prefix-local installation succeeds, then assert that the resulting ClawPatch command is user-local and reports version 0.7.2.
minimumFixScope: Change the ClawPatch installation branch in scripts/install.sh to use a prefix below install_root and update PATH or command resolution accordingly.
